subproblems.title: Gram determinant bound det(v_i·v_j) ≤ exp(Σ|v_a|² − n)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and all vectors v_1, …, v_n ∈ ℝ^P, the Gram determinant satisfies det(v_i·v_j)_{i,j=1}^n ≤ exp(Σ_{a=1}^n |v_a|² − n). (For n = 0 the determinant of the empty matrix is 1 and the right-hand side is exp(0) = 1.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)) ≤ Real.exp (∑ a, ‖v a‖ ^ 2 - (n : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of Submission.dimred_cdg_pushforward_massOn_le_first_variation): det G = Πλ_a ≤ Π e^{λ_a − 1} = exp(tr G − n). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.fvmb_gram_det_le_exp_sum_norm_sq_sub, reused with its identical frozen type. Background: Simon Ch. 4, 1.8–1.9 (book/chapter-04.txt lines 100–113, J^M_f = (det(D_{τ_k}f·D_{τ_ℓ}f))^{1/2}) and Ch. 2, §5 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 1162–1256), where the Jacobian is the square root of such a Gram determinant. The inequality is the exponential form of the AM–GM inequality for the eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix; compare Hadamard's determinant inequality. Notation: u·w is the Euclidean inner product and G := (v_i·v_j)_{i,j=1}^n (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)).
1. Operator realizing G. Let F := ℝ^n (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) with its standard orthonormal basis e_1, …, e_n (EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Let V : F → ℝ^P be the linear map with V e_a = v_a for every a, i.e. V w = Σ_a w_a v_a (in Mathlib, (basisFun).toBasis.constr ℝ v). Let V* : ℝ^P → F be its adjoint, characterized by x·V*y = Vx·y for x ∈ F, y ∈ ℝ^P, and put S := V*∘V : F → F.
2. S is symmetric with a nonnegative quadratic form. For x, y ∈ F, x·Sy = Vx·Vy by the definition of the adjoint, and likewise Sx·y = Vx·Vy. Hence Sx·y = x·Sy, and x·Sx = |Vx|² ≥ 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.isSymmetric_adjoint_comp_self).
3. Matrix, determinant and trace of S. In the orthonormal basis (e_a), the (a, b) entry of the matrix of S is e_a·Se_b = Ve_a·Ve_b = v_a·v_b = G_{ab}. So the matrix of S in this basis is G, and det S = det G, because the determinant of an endomorphism equals the determinant of its matrix in any basis (LinearMap.det_toMatrix). Also trace S = Σ_a e_a·Se_a (trace in an orthonormal basis, LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner) = Σ_a Ve_a·Ve_a = Σ_a |v_a|².
4. Spectral theorem. S is symmetric on the n-dimensional real inner product space F (finrank F = n). So there are an orthonormal basis u_1, …, u_n of F and real numbers λ_1, …, λ_n with Su_i = λ_i u_i, det S = Π_i λ_i and trace S = Σ_i λ_i. (Mathlib: LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues, eigenvectorBasis, apply_eigenvectorBasis, det_eq_prod_eigenvalues and IsSymmetric.trace_eq_sum_eigenvalues.)
5. Nonnegativity: λ_i = λ_i|u_i|² = u_i·(λ_i u_i) = u_i·Su_i = |Vu_i|² ≥ 0, by step 2.
6. Exponential AM–GM. For every real s, s + 1 ≤ e^s (Real.add_one_le_exp); with s = λ_i − 1 this gives λ_i ≤ e^{λ_i − 1}. Since 0 ≤ λ_i ≤ e^{λ_i − 1} for every i, multiplying these n inequalities between nonnegative numbers gives Π_i λ_i ≤ Π_i e^{λ_i − 1} = exp(Σ_i (λ_i − 1)) = exp(Σ_i λ_i − n) (Finset.prod_le_prod₀, Real.exp_sum).
7. Conclusion: det G = det S = Π_i λ_i ≤ exp(trace S − n) = exp(Σ_a |v_a|² − n). For n = 0 every product is empty and every sum is 0, so the same argument gives 1 ≤ exp 0 = 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Realize G = (v_i·v_j) as the matrix of the symmetric operator S = V*V on ℝ^n (V e_a = v_a) in the standard orthonormal basis, so det S = det G and tr S = Σ_a |v_a|².
Spectral theorem for S: det S = Π λ_i, tr S = Σ λ_i, and λ_i = |V u_i|² ≥ 0 for the orthonormal eigenvectors u_i.
0 ≤ λ_i ≤ e^{λ_i − 1}; multiplying these nonnegative inequalities gives Π λ_i ≤ exp(Σ λ_i − n).

subproblems.title: Uniform first-order upper bound for the Jacobian of a perturbation of the identity (Simon Ch. 2, §5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, A ≥ 0 and ε > 0. Then there exist η > 0 and δ > 0 such that the following holds for every real t with |t| < δ, all continuous linear maps B, L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with ‖B‖ ≤ A and ‖L − I − tB‖ ≤ η|t| (operator norms), and every orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n in ℝ^P: (det(Lτ_i·Lτ_j)_{i,j=1}^n)^{1/2} ≤ 1 + t Σ_{a=1}^n τ_a·Bτ_a + ε|t|. The square root is the real square root (Real.sqrt).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ A → 0 < ε → ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, |t| < δ → ∀ B L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P, ‖B‖ ≤ A → ‖L - ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) - t • B‖ ≤ η * |t| → ∀ τ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ τ → Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (L (τ i)) (L (τ j)))) ≤ 1 + t * ∑ a, inner ℝ (τ a) (B (τ a)) + ε * |t|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of Submission.dimred_cdg_pushforward_massOn_le_first_variation). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.fvmb_orthonormal_gram_sqrt_det_le_first_order, reused with its identical frozen type. Background: Simon Ch. 2, §5 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 1162–1256), where the Jacobian J_t = (det(D_{τ_i}φ_t·D_{τ_j}φ_t))^{1/2} of a variation is expanded as 1 + t div_M X + O(t²), giving the first variation formula 5.3; and Ch. 4, 1.9 and 2.1–2.3 (book/chapter-04.txt lines 100–150). Simon's printed computation is a Taylor expansion for C² families. Here, as in the parent proof, only the first-order control ‖L − I − tB‖ ≤ η|t| is available. So the estimate is one-sided, comes from the sibling's exponential bound, and is uniform in the frame. Write GE for the sibling gram_det_exp_bound (Submission.fvmb_gram_det_le_exp_sum_norm_sq_sub): for all w_1, …, w_n ∈ ℝ^P, det(w_i·w_j) ≤ exp(Σ_a |w_a|² − n). Norms of linear maps are operator norms, and u·w is the Euclidean inner product.
1. Constants.
- c₀ := (n + 1)(A + 2 + (A + 1)²) > 0 and K := n(A + 1)²/2 + c₀² > 0 (using A ≥ 0).
- η := min(1, ε/(2n + 1)) > 0 and δ := min(1, 1/c₀, ε/(2K)) > 0.
- Then η ≤ 1, and nη ≤ nε/(2n + 1) ≤ ε/2 because 2n ≤ 2n + 1. The numbers η and δ depend only on n, A and ε.
2. Setup. Fix t with |t| < δ, continuous linear maps B, L with ‖B‖ ≤ A and ‖L − I − tB‖ ≤ η|t|, and an orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n. Put:
- E := L − I − tB, so ‖E‖ ≤ η|t|;
- w_a := tBτ_a + Eτ_a, so Lτ_a = τ_a + w_a;
- D := Σ_a τ_a·Bτ_a and G := (Lτ_i·Lτ_j)_{i,j}.
From |t| < δ: |t| ≤ 1, |t| ≤ 1/c₀, |t| ≤ ε/(2K), and t² = |t|·|t| ≤ |t|.
3. Elementary bounds, from Cauchy–Schwarz, |τ_a| = 1 and |Mv| ≤ ‖M‖|v|:
- |τ_a·Bτ_a| ≤ |τ_a||Bτ_a| ≤ ‖B‖ ≤ A, hence |D| ≤ nA;
- τ_a·Eτ_a ≤ |τ_a||Eτ_a| ≤ ‖E‖ ≤ η|t|;
- |w_a| ≤ |t||Bτ_a| + |Eτ_a| ≤ |t|A + η|t| ≤ (A + 1)|t| (as η ≤ 1), hence |w_a|² ≤ (A + 1)²t².
4. One column: |Lτ_a|² = |τ_a + w_a|² = |τ_a|² + 2τ_a·w_a + |w_a|² = 1 + 2t(τ_a·Bτ_a) + 2(τ_a·Eτ_a) + |w_a|² ≤ 1 + 2t(τ_a·Bτ_a) + 2η|t| + (A + 1)²t².
5. Trace bound. Summing step 4 over a = 1, …, n gives Σ_a |Lτ_a|² − n ≤ 2tD + 2nη|t| + n(A + 1)²t² = 2σ, where σ := tD + nη|t| + n(A + 1)²t²/2.
6. Gram bound. GE applied to the n vectors Lτ_1, …, Lτ_n, together with monotonicity of exp and step 5, gives det G ≤ exp(Σ_a |Lτ_a|² − n) ≤ exp(2σ). The real square root (Real.sqrt, which is 0 on negative numbers) is monotone on all of ℝ, and √(exp(2σ)) = √(exp(σ)²) = exp(σ). Hence √(det G) ≤ exp(σ).
7. Size of σ. The triangle inequality with |D| ≤ nA, 0 < η ≤ 1, t² ≤ |t| and 1/2 ≤ 1 gives |σ| ≤ |t|·nA + n|t| + n(A + 1)²|t| = n(A + 1 + (A + 1)²)|t|. Since 0 ≤ n ≤ n + 1 and 0 ≤ A + 1 + (A + 1)² ≤ A + 2 + (A + 1)², this is ≤ (n + 1)(A + 2 + (A + 1)²)|t| = c₀|t|. Since |t| ≤ 1/c₀, |σ| ≤ 1; also σ² = |σ|² ≤ c₀²t².
8. Exponential expansion. For |σ| ≤ 1 one has |e^σ − 1 − σ| ≤ σ² (Mathlib Real.abs_exp_sub_one_sub_id_le). So e^σ ≤ 1 + σ + σ² ≤ 1 + tD + nη|t| + n(A + 1)²t²/2 + c₀²t² = 1 + tD + nη|t| + Kt².
9. Error terms. nη|t| ≤ (ε/2)|t| by step 1. Also Kt² = (K|t|)|t| ≤ (K·ε/(2K))|t| = (ε/2)|t|, because |t| ≤ ε/(2K) and K > 0.
10. Conclusion. By steps 6, 8 and 9, √(det G) ≤ e^σ ≤ 1 + tD + (ε/2)|t| + (ε/2)|t| = 1 + t Σ_a τ_a·Bτ_a + ε|t|. For n = 0 the same argument applies verbatim: the sums are empty, D = 0, σ = 0, the empty matrix has determinant 1, and GE gives 1 ≤ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose η = min(1, ε/(2n+1)) and δ = min(1, 1/c₀, ε/(2K)) with c₀ = (n+1)(A+2+(A+1)²) and K = n(A+1)²/2 + c₀².
Expand |Lτ_a|² with Lτ_a = τ_a + tBτ_a + Eτ_a, E = L − I − tB, to get Σ_a |Lτ_a|² − n ≤ 2σ with σ = tD + nη|t| + n(A+1)²t²/2 and D = Σ τ_a·Bτ_a.
The sibling Gram bound gives det G ≤ exp(2σ), hence √det G ≤ e^σ.
|σ| ≤ c₀|t| ≤ 1, so e^σ ≤ 1 + σ + σ² ≤ 1 + tD + nη|t| + Kt² ≤ 1 + tD + ε|t|.

subproblems.title: Tangential divergence in an orthonormal frame: trace(p_Q ∘ B) = Σ τ_a·Bτ_a (Simon Ch. 2, 4.20)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ_1, …, τ_n be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P whose span is the subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P. Let p_Q : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be the orthogonal projection onto Q, and let B : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be a continuous linear map. Then trace(p_Q ∘ B) = Σ_{a=1}^n τ_a·Bτ_a.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P) (B : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = Q → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (Q.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ B.toLinearMap) = ∑ a, inner ℝ (τ a) (B (τ a))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of Submission.dimred_cdg_pushforward_massOn_le_first_variation). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.fvmb_trace_starProjection_comp_eq_sum_inner, reused with its identical frozen type. Simon Ch. 2, §4, (4.18)–(4.20) (book/chapter-02.txt lines 1027–1043): div_M X = Σ_{i=1}^n τ_i·D_{τ_i}X for any orthonormal basis τ of T_yM. The contract defines tangentialDivergence n M X x as trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)), so this is exactly the identity trace(p_Q∘B) = Σ_a τ_a·Bτ_a proved here. Notation: p_Q := Q.starProjection (the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto Q, as a map ℝ^P → ℝ^P), u·w is the Euclidean inner product, and trace is LinearMap.trace.
1. Projection formula. For z ∈ ℝ^P put w(z) := Σ_a (τ_a·z)τ_a. Then w(z) ∈ span{τ_1, …, τ_n} = Q.
- For each b, orthonormality gives τ_b·(z − w(z)) = τ_b·z − Σ_a (τ_a·z)(τ_b·τ_a) = τ_b·z − τ_b·z = 0.
- The set {q : q·(z − w(z)) = 0} is a linear subspace containing every τ_b, so it contains span{τ_b} = Q (induction over the span, Submodule.span_induction).
- The orthogonal projection is characterized by: if u ∈ Q and (z − u)·q = 0 for all q ∈ Q, then p_Q z = u (Mathlib Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). Hence p_Q z = Σ_a (τ_a·z)τ_a.
2. Decomposition into rank-one maps. For a = 1, …, n let ℓ_a : ℝ^P → ℝ be the linear functional ℓ_a(z) := τ_a·Bz, and let R_a : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be the rank-one linear map R_a(z) := ℓ_a(z)τ_a (LinearMap.smulRight ℓ_a τ_a). Applying step 1 to Bz gives (p_Q∘B)z = Σ_a (τ_a·Bz)τ_a = Σ_a R_a(z) for every z. So p_Q∘B = Σ_a R_a as linear maps.
3. Trace of a rank-one map. For a linear functional ℓ and a vector v, the map R(z) = ℓ(z)v has trace ℓ(v) (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_smulRight). Directly: with the standard orthonormal basis e_1, …, e_P of ℝ^P, trace R = Σ_k e_k·Re_k = Σ_k ℓ(e_k)(e_k·v) = ℓ(Σ_k (e_k·v)e_k) = ℓ(v), by linearity of ℓ and the expansion v = Σ_k (e_k·v)e_k.
4. By linearity of the trace and steps 2–3, trace(p_Q∘B) = Σ_a trace R_a = Σ_a ℓ_a(τ_a) = Σ_a τ_a·Bτ_a.
5. For n = 0 (empty family), Q = span ∅ = {0} and p_Q = 0, so both sides are 0; the argument above covers this case with empty sums. ∎
proof_key_steps: p_Q z = Σ_a (τ_a·z)τ_a, by the orthogonality characterization of the projection onto Q = span τ.
Hence p_Q∘B = Σ_a R_a with rank-one maps R_a(z) = (τ_a·Bz)τ_a.
trace R_a = τ_a·Bτ_a, since the trace of z ↦ ℓ(z)v is ℓ(v); sum over a by linearity of the trace.

subproblems.title: The orientation of an integer multiplicity triple orients the chosen approximate tangent plane a.e.
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n). Then for H^n-almost every x ∈ M (with respect to μHE[n] restricted to M), ξ(x) is a unit orientation of approxTangentPlane n M x. That is, there are orthonormal τ_1, …, τ_n spanning approxTangentPlane n M x such that either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of Submission.dimred_cdg_pushforward_massOn_le_first_variation). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.fvmb_imrep_ae_unitOrientation_approxTangentPlane, reused with its identical frozen type. Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 733–747): for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = τ_1∧⋯∧τ_n with τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1) (book/chapter-03.txt line 86): the approximate tangent space is unique if it exists (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean:232). Write M := R.carrier, ξ := R.orient and μ := μHE[n] restricted to M.
1. By the field R.orients, for μ-almost every x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Fix such x and Q. It suffices to prove approxTangentPlane n M x = Q, because IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) (approxTangentPlane n M x) is then the second property of Q.
2. By definition, approxTangentPlane n M x is the chosen witness Q₀ of the proposition ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' when this proposition holds, and ⊥ otherwise. Here the proposition holds, with Q as a witness. So approxTangentPlane n M x = Q₀, and by the defining property of the choice, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₀.
3. Approximate tangent planes are unique: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₀ and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q imply Q₀ = Q (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Hence approxTangentPlane n M x = Q.
4. Therefore IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) (approxTangentPlane n M x) holds at every x of the full-measure set from step 1, i.e. for μ-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: R.orients gives, μHE[n]⌞M-a.e., a plane Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q that ξ(x) orients.
At such x, approxTangentPlane n M x is the chosen witness, which equals Q by HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique.
